title: Majestic Geometric Paisley Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A traditional geometric mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring lotus pattern and ring pattern. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for a wedding.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.

Moroccan and other North African henna traditions rely on lines, diamonds and triangles rather than flowers. Geometric pattern is central to Islamic art, which favours repeating, non-figurative designs.
Application tips: Draw straight lines in one steady pull instead of several short strokes. Keep line thickness consistent; uneven lines stand out more in geometric work than in florals.

image.alt: Geometric Paisley mehndi design for front hand — majestic henna pattern

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

title: Elaborate Geometric Heart Vine Mehndi Design for Foot
descriptionParagraphs: A classic geometric mehndi design tailored for the foot, featuring bell garland and checkered fill. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

The soles take henna as well as the palms do, while the top of the foot stains lighter. Stay seated and avoid walking until the paste has dried completely. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
Modern minimal mehndi often uses geometric shapes with plenty of bare skin around them. Symmetry is what makes a geometric design work, so spacing matters more than detail.

Application tips: Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain. Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.
